_note: CALIBRATION gold set A (IncidentResponse) — labels are Claude's best guess for Robert to CORRECT. Distinct domain from recipebox/apptrail and from the nine scoring visions. Each candidate carries a 'tier' tag (Spec4's _VALID_TIERS ladder; NOT sent to the judge). gold_borderline=true marks adjacent<->off_domain seams. pair_id links matched-tier pairs: the SAME relevance relationship at two tiers, which the judge should label identically (a mismatch = tier drift). Seam tags: alpha=job-derivable-but-no-phrase, beta=broad-surface-but-off-the-job.

vision.purpose: A copilot for the on-call engineer that helps them understand and resolve a production incident faster.
target_audience: On-call engineers triaging production incidents under time pressure
SRE teams who want to cut mean-time-to-resolution

incident_summary.description: Summarizes a firing alert and its recent related alerts into a one-paragraph situation brief for the responder.

runbook_answers.description: Answers 'how do we handle this' by retrieving from the team's runbooks and past post-mortems and composing a cited answer.

guided_remediation.description: With a small fixed set of tools (metrics, logs, deploy history), fetches the signals the engineer asks for and can trigger a bounded, pre-approved action such as a rollback.

candidates.name: alert_correlation_grouping
candidates.rough_description: Groups the firing alert with recent alerts that are semantically related, so the brief reflects one incident rather than twenty separate pages.
candidates.note: incident_summary cannot describe one coherent incident without knowing which alerts belong together. Necessity, cite incident_summary.

candidates.name: runbook_grounded_answer
candidates.rough_description: Retrieves the most relevant runbook and post-mortem passages for the current incident and composes a cited answer to the responder's question.
candidates.note: runbook_answers IS this mechanism. Necessity, cite runbook_answers.

candidates.name: metrics_and_logs_tool_calls
candidates.rough_description: Calls the metrics and logs tools the engineer asks for and returns the readings inline in the conversation.
candidates.note: guided_remediation's stated outcome requires fetching the requested signals. Necessity, cite guided_remediation.

candidates.name: single_pass_incident_brief
candidates.rough_description: Produces the incident situation brief in one LLM pass over the correlated alert payload.
candidates.note: Matched pair A_brief (low tier). This is a direct mechanism for incident_summary. Grounded, cite incident_summary.

candidates.name: subagent_incident_brief
candidates.rough_description: Produces the same incident situation brief by dispatching subagents that each analyze one subsystem (database, network, application) and synthesizing their findings.
candidates.note: Matched pair A_brief (high tier). Relevance to incident_summary is IDENTICAL to single_pass_incident_brief; only the mechanism/tier differs. The judge (told to ignore tier) should also label this grounded. A downgrade here = tier drift.

candidates.name: severity_classification
candidates.rough_description: Classifies the incident's severity (SEV1 to SEV4) from the alert and current signals to aid triage.
candidates.note: Serves the understand-and-triage purpose; no stated feature requires it. Enhancement.

candidates.name: post_incident_rca_pipeline
candidates.rough_description: After resolution, runs a fixed pipeline that chains extract-timeline, classify-root-cause, and draft-post-mortem to produce a first-draft post-mortem.
candidates.note: SEAM (alpha): the purpose is resolving the incident faster, with no phrase about post-mortems; but a job around the team's runbooks/post-mortems (runbook_answers) is plausibly served by generating the next one. Proposed adjacent.

candidates.name: autonomous_infra_optimizer
candidates.rough_description: An autonomous agent that continuously explores the infrastructure, forms hypotheses about cost and performance improvements, and opens pull requests to implement them.
candidates.note: SEAM (beta): the 'infrastructure' surface may tempt a phrase-anchored judge, but the vision is resolving an incident in the moment, not standing autonomous optimization; serves no incident-resolution job. Proposed off_domain.

candidates.name: oncall_rotation_scheduling
candidates.rough_description: Manages the team's on-call rotation calendar and pages the next engineer when needed.
candidates.note: Scheduling/paging is a separate product; the vision is understanding and resolving the incident in front of you. Guardrail.
